27.21: 27.21 A burning wind shall take him away. The burning wind is called the malignant spirit, who drives him whom he now inflames with the fire of perverse concupiscence afterward to the flames of Gehenna. And as a whirlwind shall snatch him. The place of the perverse is the delight of temporal life.
27.22: 27.22 And he shall cast upon him. As often as God corrects the sinner by striking, he sends this scourge in order to spare. But when by striking he concludes his life persisting in sin, he sends the scourge but by no means spares. From his hand. Because the hand is understood as operation, he flees from the hand of the stricken, who, while he sees the destruction of the wicked, leaves the ways of wickedness, hence it follows:
27.23: 27.23 He shall clap his hands. To clap the hands is to confirm the works of life in rectitude, seeing in another's punishment what to fear.
28.1: 28.1 Silver has beginnings of its veins. GREGORY. After the punishments of the powerful proud, etc., down to that they be strengthened by no authority of the sacred books. And there is a place for gold. In this place the heretics, etc., down to first here has burned in the workshop of charity.
28.2: 28.2 Iron is taken out of the earth. Heretics are wont to glory in justice, and accuse Catholics of having been unjust. Against whom, through humble confession, it is said: Iron is taken out of the earth. Because stronger men are separated from the earthly action which they held before, and become defenders of the Church. And the stone melted. Because the hard heart, etc., down to and by preaching becomes sonorous.
28.3: 28.3 He has set a time for darkness. The unjust, namely, a measure by which the unjust may cease to be unjust. And of all. Because he looks upon the end of the elect, etc., down to that it blinded itself with the darkness of hardened perfidy. The stone also of darkness. The people of the Jews hard in perfidy, etc., down to expressed his image in itself.
28.4: 28.4 The torrent divides from the people. Ibid. By the name of torrent, etc., down to by the name of torrent can be understood the irrigation of holy preaching. Those whom he forgot, that is the Jews, etc., down to because by the words of life they would not give a way to the heart.
28.5: 28.5 The land out of which bread. Because Judea both first had the law to refresh, and afterward, the miracles of the Redeemer being seen, envy to burn up.
28.6: 28.6 The place of sapphire are its stones. Ibid. Sapphires are of the color of air. And he says this, because there never lacked from Judea holy souls who led a heavenly life: And its clods. By clods he means the gatherings of the several orders, etc., down to But why it lost the good, it follows:
28.7: 28.7 The path no bird knew. In this place by the name of bird that one is signified, etc., down to would not consider. Nor has the eye beheld. Our Redeemer of the vulture, etc., down to of whom it is added:
28.8: 28.8 The children of the merchants have not trodden it. The merchants are those who conduct spiritual business, etc., down to the sons of merchants, pastors and teachers. Nor has the lioness passed by it. The Church is called lioness, because she slays those living badly in vices with the mouth of holy preaching, hence it is said to Peter: Kill and eat. The Church therefore passed through Judea, but did not pass entirely: because she snatched few from it to the faith, yet did not utterly extinguish the unbelieving people from perfidy. But being repulsed by the Jews, what did she do?
28.9: 28.9 He has stretched forth his hand to the flint. Because to the hardness of the Gentiles he sent the arm of his preaching. He has overturned the mountains from the roots. The roots, the inmost thoughts of the proud: the mountains were overturned from the roots, because the powers of the world fell away from the inmost thought to worshiping God.
28.10: 28.10 In the rocks he has cut out rivers, etc. Ibid. That is, in the hard hearts of the Gentiles he opened streams of preaching. And his eye has seen every precious thing. God saw the precious thing when he looked upon the human soul, cast away from itself, by the illumination of the wisdom of his grace.
28.11: 28.11 The depths also. The Lord searches the depths of the rivers, etc., down to and by no merit of ours the wisdom of God comes to us.
28.13: 28.13 Neither is it found in the land. By land he means the human soul. This wisdom cannot be found in the land of those living pleasantly, because whoever is still fed with the pleasures of this life is separated from the understanding of eternal wisdom.
28.14: 28.14 The depth says. The depth he calls the hearts of men, etc., down to which says foolish things with God by wicked works. The sea speaks: not, the minds of the restless, etc., down to but would come through itself. It follows:
28.15: 28.15 The finest gold shall not be given for it. The holy angels are called the finest gold, etc., down to but not without contagion of guilt. Nor shall silver be weighed in exchange for it. Because the life of the just who preach, or write the words of God, however much it abounds in the light of holiness, does not communicate to us by its presence the coming of the heavenly wisdom.
28.16: 28.16 It shall not be compared with the dyed colors of India. By India this world is understood, etc., down to and a garment without dye. Nor to the sardonyx stone. The sardonyx holds the likeness of red earth, the sapphire an airy appearance: by sardonyx therefore men, or the fathers of the Old Testament following some earthly things; by sapphire the preachers of the New Testament seeking heavenly things alone, or angels are understood.
28.17: 28.17 Gold or glass shall not equal it. GREGORY. After it was said, etc., down to because they are creatures. Nor shall vessels be exchanged for it. The lofty vessel of gold, etc., down to but believes the Lord of the prophets.
28.18: 28.18 High and eminent things shall not be remembered in comparison. For what are men compared to God? Nothing. But wisdom is drawn. Because since it is invisible, etc., down to And you know not whence it comes or whither it goes.
28.19: 28.19 The topaz shall not equal it. Because it shines with every color, etc., down to which he shows when he adds: Nor the cleanest dyeing. The cleanest dyeings are those who humbly keep the grace of virtues coming upon them. For they would not be dyed if they had holiness by nature.
28.20: 28.20 Whence then comes wisdom? Because it is born of the invisible Father, etc., down to and which is the place of understanding?
28.21: 28.21 It is hid. Because as long as one lives here God cannot be seen by the appearance of his nature; by images, however, he was seen by Moses, Jacob and others. It is hid also from the fowls of the air. GREGORY on Job, book 19. Because set in this corruptible flesh, etc., down to in their sayings and consolations they breathe from the weariness of this life.
28.22: 28.22 Destruction and death have said, etc. Ibid. Because to see God is what it is to have him: therefore the wicked see not this wisdom, because, repelled by pride, they could in no way have it. To have heard the fame of it is to have known his power from his virtue.
28.23: 28.23 God understands the way. As if to say, etc., down to in all parts of the world would fill the hearts of the elect. It follows:
28.24: 28.24 For he beholds the ends of the world. The looking of God is to restore the lost to grace.
28.25: 28.25 Who made a weight for the winds. By the swiftness and loftiness of the winds, etc., down to to temper glory with mixed weakness. And weighed the waters, etc. Ibid. By waters he means minds by the Holy Spirit, etc., down to but flees the woman, struck with fear.
28.26: 28.26 When he gave a law to the rains. The rain, the sayings of the preachers, etc., down to which preserves in work what it sounded.
28.27: 28.27 Then he saw it, and declared it. This incarnate wisdom he saw, that is made to be seen, and declared, made to be prepared by preachers and searched out by hearers. For he prepares it for himself, whoever has cared to have it propitious in the day of judgment by living well. He saw it, etc. He saw, because it is a species, etc., down to what man would know of it in himself, hence it is added:
28.28: 28.28 And he said to man, etc. Because we cannot penetrate the nature of wisdom what it is in itself: by the condescension of God we have heard what it is in us. For it is certain that he has it whose fear of God is not uncertain. Behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, etc., as if he said If you fear God, it is plain that you are full of wisdom which in man is called the fear of the Lord. But because he truly understands the force of divine fear who keeps himself from all wicked works, he adds: And to depart from evil is understanding.
29.1: 29.1 Job added also, etc. Ibid. In this last discourse, etc., down to that he longs with a sigh for these our wretched times, hence he says:
29.2: 29.2 Who will grant me to be, etc. The fixed number of days is called months, etc., down to when the error that is now hidden shall be open. The months past. Days, when they are gathered, are subtracted in months; because the Church, while she gathers shining souls, hides them in the inmost. Or, month is put for perfection, which shall be to them in rest to whom it is now in operation, which the Church now remembers. According to the days, etc. Because she will then think herself to fall in those failing from persecution who now sees herself kept in these.
29.3: 29.3 When his lamp shined, etc. The lamp is called the light of sacred Scripture. Now therefore the lamp shines above the head of the Church, because the sacred words irradiate the darkness of our mind. And by his light, etc. Ibid. The Church, though she does not penetrate the secrets of another's thought, because she does not know the face of God by night, yet sets the steps of good work by the direct light of heavenly speech.
29.4: 29.4 As I was in the days of my youth. The Church was grown up, etc., down to when by preaching she cannot bring forth children. When God was secret in my tabernacle. The tabernacle a dwelling, etc., down to When the Almighty was with me. It follows: And round about, etc. Boys are called those who serve the heavenly commands, who now are round about her, because they are found in almost all nations.
29.6: 29.6 When I washed my feet. The feet of the Church are the ministers of lower works, etc., down to the feet are those who minister outward things. And the rock poured out for me, etc. Ibid. Because in her the preachings of Christ of inmost anointing flow forth. From this rock came rivers of oil the books of the evangelists; or the rivers of oil he calls the gifts of the Spirit.
29.7: 29.7 When I went forth, etc. By the gate of the city, etc., down to which Job also did. And in the street they prepared, etc. Because in the breadth of great authority he exhibits the freedom of his teaching. For he who preaches in public voice the right things he feels sits as it were in the street on the chair, when he fears nothing of his preaching, and no one, pressed by terrors, hides himself in silence.
29.8: 29.8 The young men saw me, etc. Young men he says, because the old are not upheld by any gravity of counsel, ripe in the age of morals. And the sense is: The immature dread the vigor and rectitude of the Church, and the aged glorify it.
29.9: 29.9 The princes ceased to speak. By princes or leaders he means the authors of heretical depravity. And the sense is: When it was lawful for me to preach in public voice, everyone not subject to the truth feared me. They lay the finger on the mouth, while by false complaints they signify that they are repressed not by reason of the voice but by the hand of power.
29.10: 29.10 The leaders held back their voice. Surely these who try to draw the wandering peoples after them, etc., down to while they insinuate perverse things, they confirm in impiety by nourishing.
29.11: 29.11 The ear that heard. There he said, what he showed by doctrine, etc., down to who answers by the examples of his life by living well.
29.12: 29.12 Because I delivered the poor man crying out. The Church delivers the poor man crying out, when she relaxes to the sinner begging pardon the faults he committed. And the fatherless that had no helper. She delivers the fatherless while each, etc., down to The Church does this also bodily and spiritually.
29.13: 29.13 The blessing of him that was ready to perish. GREGORY. The blessing of him ready to perish comes upon her when she prevents the destruction of the sinner and by holy exhortations leads him back from the pit of guilt. And I comforted the heart of the widow. The heart of the widow receives great consolation, when the faithful soul in the words of the Church recognizes something of the coming of him to whom she is spiritually joined.
29.14: 29.14 I was clothed with justice. He is clothed with justice as with a garment, etc., down to who is lifted up from the fault he overcomes. And my judgment as a diadem. The judgment of the just is called a diadem, because through it they seek reward not in earthly and weak things but above. I was clothed with judgment: which is compared to a crown placed above, because he seeks to be crowned in heaven, not on earth. He opens his goods, that friends may not be rebuked but raised up, but may imitate in silence. The memory of former things also avails against despair on account of rebukes.
29.15: 29.15 I was an eye to the blind and a foot to the lame, etc. For blessed Job both held out a hand to them himself, etc., down to who is evil to himself, to whom is he good?
29.16: 29.16 I was the father of the poor. For the poor in spirit are begotten by his preaching. And the cause which I knew not. The Church, when through the elect evils, etc., down to yet lesser things are to be left for the greater.
29.17: 29.17 I broke the jaws, etc. The unjust is called the devil; by the jaws his hidden snares; by the teeth the accomplishment of open guilt is shown. First therefore it is necessary to betray the hidden contrivances of his counsels, that we may be able to recall the soul of our hearer in open fall.
29.18: 29.18 And I said: I shall die in my nest. By the name of nest is expressed, etc., down to nor, as some, to do more at the beginning, less at the consummation.
29.19: 29.19 My root, etc. Ibid. The root of the Church is Christ incarnate, down to the thought of the mind is opened And dew shall abide, etc. Understand I said, etc., down to that we may be worthy, to be gathered from the lower.
29.20: 29.20 My glory shall always be renewed. The same laments as lost glory, because those whom he believed to serve in the warfare of the new life he sees serving old desires. And my bow. Scripture is the bow, etc., down to which even now is.
29.21: 29.21 They that heard me. She remembers past times, in which all that is said by her is heard with fear by the faithful, and she laments the insolence of adversaries. And they were silent intent. At her counsel they are silent, who dare not impugn her words but believe.
